title: Integrated Finance Policy: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement and Revenue Recognition (2026 Q2)
author: Laura Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's core financial policies and operational procedures for budgeting and forecasting, contracts and legal review, procurement approvals, and revenue recognition / billing practices. It is intended as the single-point reference for finance, legal, procurement, and product teams when executing spend commitments, negotiating contracts, and recording revenue.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood entities and product lines.
- Covers capital and operating budgets, vendor contracting lifecycle, purchasing procedures, approval thresholds, and basic revenue recognition rules used by Finance for month-end and quarter-end close.

Owners and Contacts
- Document owner: Finance (owner_team: finance-legal)
- Finance lead: Laura Chen (finance@redwoodinference.com)
- Legal review: Marcus Owens (legal@redwoodinference.com)
- Procurement coordinator: Nina Rodriguez (procurement@redwoodinference.com)

1) Budgeting and Forecasting

Summary
Redwood runs an annual operating budget (AOB) and rolling 12-month forecast updated monthly. Budget authority is delegated to functional leads; variance reporting and reforecast triggers are defined below.

Key controls and cadence
- Annual budget cycle: planning kickoff in August, departmental submissions in September, executive review October, Board approval by November.
- Monthly close and reforecast: finance issues a rolling 12-month forecast template by the 3rd business day of each month; teams return inputs by the 7th.
- Variance thresholds triggering escalation:
  1. >10% variance to headcount or opex line item for two consecutive months -> automatic review with Finance and People Ops.
  2. >15% variance to monthly revenue or gross margin -> product + finance deep-dive.

Approval matrix (budget-level)
- Team lead: approves within-team re-allocations under $25k annualized.
- Department head: approves budget changes up to $250k annualized.
- CFO: approves changes > $250k.
- Executive Committee: approval required for changes > $1M or material scope changes to product roadmaps.

Budget templates and artifacts
- Use the canonical AOB Google Sheet (link internal) and the monthly forecast workbook.
- Required attachments for material changes (> $250k): business case, ROI estimate, implementation timeline, and owner signoff.

2) Contracts and Legal Process

Policy summary
All customer-facing contracts, reseller agreements, partnership contracts, and critical vendor contracts must follow the standard contract lifecycle and receive Legal review prior to signature. Finance must be looped on contracts with billing, revenue share, or MSA/enterprise terms.

Contract lifecycle (step-by-step)
1. Request / intake: Originating team fills the Contract Intake form and uploads initial draft.
2. Legal review: Legal assigns a reviewer within 48 business hours for standard templates. Complex or high-risk contracts (see risk table) are escalated to senior counsel.
3. Commercial review: Finance verifies pricing, billing cadence, revenue recognition implications, and any revenue share or discount schedules.
4. Sign-off: Required signatories based on contract type (table below).
5. Execution & storage: Fully executed contracts are uploaded to the contract repository (DocStore) and tagged with contract metadata (counterparty, start/end, renewal terms, owner, cost center).

Signatory authority table
- Up to $250k ARR or 12-month term: VP / Director of the originating function + Finance business partner.
- >$250k to $1M: CFO approval required.
- >$1M or strategic enterprise deals with indemnity/data-residency clauses: CEO approval + Legal Director.

Standard clauses and redlines
- Use standard Redwood MSA and SOW templates where possible.
- Data residency, indemnity, liability caps and security clauses require Legal review. Typical liability cap: lesser of $5M or 12 months of fees unless approved by Legal & Exec.

Contract review timelines
- Standard template review: 2-3 business days.
- Non-standard or vendor contracts: 5-10 business days.

3) Procurement Procedures

Objective
Ensure procurement of goods and services follows competitive, documented, and approved processes to control spend and mitigate vendor risk.

Procurement request flow
1. Requestor opens Purchase Requisition (PR) in the procurement portal including business justification, budget code, and proposed vendor.
2. Procurement team obtains quotes (required thresholds below).
3. Finance verifies budget availability.
4. Approval chain executes; Procurement issues Purchase Order (PO) and tracks delivery.

Competitive sourcing thresholds
- <$5k: single quote; team lead approval required.
- $5k- $50k: two written quotes required; department head approval.
- >$50k to $250k: three quotes and procurement + finance approval.
- >$250k: RFP required, procurement-led sourcing, and CFO approval.

Vendor onboarding checklist
- Completed W-9 or local tax form.
- Proof of insurance where required.
- Security questionnaire for vendors with data access.
- Contract uploaded and noted in Vendor Registry.

Payment terms and preferred cadence
- Standard vendor terms: Net 30. Purchasing team negotiates Net 45/60 only with documented business rationale and CFO approval.
- Preferred payment methods: ACH (primary), corporate card for incidental spend (policy caps apply).

4) Revenue Recognition and Billing Policies

Principles
Revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC 606: identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, recognize when control transfers. The following are Redwood-specific rules to operationalize ASC 606 for product and services revenue.

Product / Hosted API revenue
- Subscription/commit pricing: Recognize ratably over the contract term unless evidence shows distinct performance obligations with different timing.
- Usage/overage billing: Recognize when usage is billed or when measurement indicates earned revenue; for invoiced usage, revenue is recognized in the period the usage was incurred.

Professional services and implementation
- Implementation SOWs with distinct deliverables: recognize upon delivery / acceptance of the deliverable.
- Time-and-materials: recognize as services are performed.

Deferred revenue and billing cadence
- Upfront annual prepayments: recognized ratably; deferred revenue liability established on cash receipt.
- Monthly/weekly usage billing: billed monthly; revenue recognized in the corresponding month.
- Credits / refunds: applied in the billing period they are issued. Material credits that affect multiple periods should be amortized and discussed with Accounting.

Invoicing standards
- Standard customers: invoice within 5 business days after month-end for usage and recurring charges.
- Enterprise customers: follow contract-specific billing schedules; billing exceptions must be documented and approved by Finance.
- Invoices to include: contract ID, billing period, detailed usage (if applicable), tax treatment, PO number (if supplied).

Revenue cutoffs and close procedures
- Cutoff rule: recognize revenue for services performed up to and including the last calendar day of the reporting period. For usage-based revenue, use meter readings and system logs aligned to period boundaries.
- Monthly close checklist: invoices generated, deferred revenue schedules updated, revenue recognition entries posted, and revenue variance summary prepared for review.

5) Controls, Audit and Reporting

Key controls
- Contract repository: 100% of executed contracts must be stored in DocStore within 3 business days of execution.
- Segregation of duties: Procurement cannot both approve and pay the same invoice.
- Budget-to-actual reconciliation: departmental owners must reconcile and approve monthly spend reports within 10 business days of month close.

Audit readiness
- Finance will produce supporting schedules for all revenue recognized and deferred balances at quarter-end.
- Contract and procurement audit trail (intake form, approvals, PO, invoice) must be maintained for 7 years.

6) Exceptions and Escalation

Common exceptions
- Urgent procurement for critical infrastructure (e.g., emergency cloud capacity) may be processed with expedited approvals but must be documented and retrospectively validated by Procurement and Finance within 5 business days.
- Contract terms deviating from standard playbooks (e.g., custom indemnity) require Legal Director and CFO pre-approval.

Escalation path
1. Responsible owner -> Procurement / Finance -> Legal (if contract terms) -> CFO -> Exec Committee (if unresolved).

Appendices
A. Quick reference approval thresholds (table)
| Action | Approval required | Notes |
|--------|-------------------|-------|
| Purchase < $5k | Team lead | Single quote |
| $5k- $50k | Department head + 2 quotes | Documented quotes in PR |
| $50k- $250k | Procurement + Finance | 3 quotes, justification |
| > $250k | CFO + Procurement-led RFP | Board notification for > $1M |

B. Contract metadata fields required in DocStore
- Counterparty name
- Contract owner (function + person)
- Start date / end date / renewal terms
- Billing frequency and contract ID
- Liability limits and any non-standard security or data terms

C. Common templates and links
- Standard MSA, SOW, and Procurement PO templates (internal links).
- Contract Intake form (internal link).
- Monthly forecast workbook (internal link).

D. Frequently asked questions
- Q: Who signs recurring subscription contracts for small customers?
  A: Director-level signatory for up to $250k ARR (see Signatory authority table).
- Q: How are prepayments treated?
  A: Recognized ratably over the contractual period; cash receipt recorded as deferred revenue until recognized.

Change log
- 2026-04-15: Document created and published (Laura Chen).
- 2026-06-10: Minor updates to procurement thresholds and contract review SLA (reviewers: Marcus Owens, Nina Rodriguez).

Related resources
- Finance playbooks, procurement portal, DocStore contract repository, monthly forecast template (internal links).

Notes
This guidance is intended to provide practical controls and steps that align commercial and operational teams with Finance and Legal. For ambiguous situations, consult Legal (legal@redwoodinference.com) and Finance (finance@redwoodinference.com) before execution.
